description: Overnight runs on a local model (tiiny): a retry or a new run continues the ticket's leftover branch instead of starting from base, and a pi provider error (e.g. a 404 because -m does not match the loaded model) stops the run instead of burning the queue. Source: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-20-tiiny-overnight-design.md and the plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-20-tiiny-overnight.md (read the plan's Global Constraints and Review Focus before each story). Only runWavesIsolated (the git path) changes; runWaves (no git) is out of scope. The adversarial resume path (detectResume) keeps priority over continuing a branch. Tests assert exit codes, files, git state, ticket Status and recorded prompts compared against exported rule constants, never prose wording.

userStories.title: continueWorktree checks out a ticket branch as it is
userStories.description: As a redeye developer, I want a queued function that checks out an existing ticket branch without resetting it and merges the base in when the base has moved, so that a later attempt can build on earlier work. (Plan Task 1.)
acceptanceCriteria: src/worktree.ts exports type ContinuedWorktree = { worktreePath, branchName, base:'up-to-date'|'merged'|'conflict' } and continueWorktree(opts:{ repoRoot, repoName, baseBranch, ticket }):Promise<ContinuedWorktree>
The worktree path computation used by createWorktree is extracted into one shared helper that both functions call; it is not copied
continueWorktree checks the branch out through addWorktreeForBranch (which runs on worktreeQueue), so it never resets the branch
When baseBranch is already an ancestor of the branch head, base is 'up-to-date' and the branch head is unchanged
Otherwise it runs git merge --no-edit <baseBranch> in the worktree; on success base is 'merged'
On a merge failure it runs git merge --abort and returns base 'conflict'; the worktree is clean and the branch head equals the head before the call
Test in test/worktree.test.ts 'continueWorktree keeps the branch commits': a file committed on the ticket branch exists in the returned worktree, base is 'up-to-date', branch head unchanged
Test 'continueWorktree merges a base that moved': a later commit on base and the branch's commit both appear in the worktree, base is 'merged'
Test 'continueWorktree leaves the branch alone on a conflict': branch and base both change line 1 of the same file; base is 'conflict', isDirty(worktreePath) is false, branch head unchanged
Every test repo sets user.name and user.email in its own git config

userStories.title: piTurnError reads one pi stream line
userStories.description: As a redeye developer, I want a pure function that classifies one parsed pi JSON line as an error turn, a successful turn, or irrelevant, so that spawnAgent can tell when the agent ended on a provider error. (Plan Task 3, pure half.)
